title: fix: let guests mark owned conversations unread
body: Fixes #173925. ## What Problem This Solves Guests with session-write access cannot mark their own conversations unread: the Actions menu disables the item and asks for the broader `operator.write` scope. The same mismatch in the action and automatic-read callers would prevent a complete unread/read cycle even if the menu alone were enabled. ## User Impact Session writers can use unread reminders on their existing owned conversations from the sidebar, chat header, and sessions list, then mark them read explicitly or by reopening the chat. Foreign conversations remain protected by the existing ownership check; read-only access and unavailable methods remain disabled. Broad-write and administrator behavior is retained. Manual unread markers keep their existing timestamp protection, and implicit acknowledgement of folded hidden runs remains conditional. The change adds no permission, configuration, schema, or persistence contract. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway already admits ordinary owned-session organization through `operator.sessions.write`. The Control UI permission resolver supports that alternative when a scoped consumer opts in, but unread callers were selecting its broad default. This change passes the existing scope option at those consumers and supplies the existing session ownership fact to automatic acknowledgement. Other appearance, grouping, assignment, and privileged actions keep their present access requirements. The shared authorization resolver and Gateway remain unchanged. ## Evidence The existing session organizer harness fails against the original production code with `This action requires operator.write access.` under a narrow session-write grant. Remote validation passed 143 focused owner/caller tests, changed-file formatting/lint and UI translation verification, and all 11 selected type graphs. The focused test command took 17.77 seconds wall time. After correcting the browser test to target the active retained pane and wait for menu closure, all 4 cases in `ui/src/e2e/session-management.operator-scopes.e2e.test.ts` passed (21.07 seconds command wall; 19.31 seconds Vitest duration). The scenario exercises sessions-list unread, automatic acknowledgement on reopening, sidebar unread, header read, and continued foreign-session denial. The correction also passed changed-file checks and the affected E2E type graph. A refreshed focused batch passed 51 organizer/menu cases, 21 read-marker cases, and 23 existing Gateway narrow-mutation cases. The Gateway tests call the production request dispatcher and mutation handler, revoke requester authority or replace the target generation while the request waits, and verify that `markedUnreadAt` remains absent in storage. These are isolated production-boundary fixtures. The actual authenticated guest UI also passed owned unread, explicit read, ordinary revisit acknowledgement, disabled foreign-session unread controls, and continued restriction of unrelated broad-write actions. The six affected production files match the combined development runtime; original build stamps are retained. The two dashboard failures in the [initial CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38864461021) also occur on the [scheduled-main baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38863277510): the restored widget border is 0px instead of 1px, and the restored website iframe times out. The 26 relevant owner, fixture, style, dependency and runner inputs are unchanged; those admin-scoped dashboard flows do not use the changed narrow unread actions. Those stale dashboard expectations were subsequently corrected on main in #171664 and #173929; the fresh dashboard shard passes. Those repairs are separate from this contribution. The independent review is clean on the corrected head, and the exact-head ClawSweeper review is Platinum with no actionable findings. The current hosted run still fails one sidebar owner-assignment case because its “Me” menu item did not become visible within 30 seconds. The same 96-file inventory passed all 409 cases on both the exact CI parent and the exact CI merge, with the previously failing case completing in 1.81 and 1.84 seconds respectively. These diagnostic replays do not establish the timeout’s cause or prove a fix. The original job uploaded only its sanitized state report; its private screenshot was not retained in the downloadable artifacts. The hosted failure and its aggregate gate remain unresolved. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Own\-session Mark as unread is disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92565632-647c-4c12-8863-e8af300b78bc) | ![Own\-session Mark as unread is enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66200fb4-f2f2-499b-b00b-1a8e84f288b8) | ### Actual guest interaction; orange outline indicates the clicked control https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0dd30da4-b8ef-4d10-987c-08dc4693c2f5 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 17fedf5b0bd3639f8058e6baba053a2987c93061 - Exact head: `21b5fe389a1e1e72e58043244a7589ab46ea9fc2` - Scenario: Mark an owned conversation unread, verify the inverse action, then clear it manually and by revisiting\. - Runtime/build: Local OpenClaw development runtime, producer bbc3b1f869937f164b3b6ecc905dc03cfc054c8c; source\-equivalent affected files; original build stamps preserved\. - Observed result: Mark as unread sets the sidebar marker and offers Mark as read - Observed result: Manual read and ordinary revisit clear the marker - Observed result: Another guest session stays disabled; broad write actions remain disabled - Actual authenticated guest UI, retained session and workspace - Before and after captures use the same browser viewport and theme; cropped to the affected surface - Timestamped actual screenshot\-stream frames; private surroundings redacted - Affected author files match the combined runtime; test\-only corrections preserve production bytes - The brief interval while the menu is closed is covered to exclude unrelated private conversation text; source frames retained
